title: Polyglot SDK: declarative tool registries + incremental JSON framing examples
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: Goal: Provide concrete, ergonomic examples and interface contracts for TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs that support: 1) streaming text + evented partial-JSON emissions; 2) first-class tool/function registration with declarative registries; 3) schema-driven structured outputs with per-request validators; and 4) compatibility shims so older clients keep working. Deliverables: a) API surface proposal for each language, b) sample snippets demonstrating progressive JSON emissions ("partial object" patches + reconciliation token), c) compatibility notes and migration guidance, and d) tests and a small reference app that exercises tool invocation routing and fallback model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Clear TS/Py/Go interface signatures for streaming + tool registration
Working examples in each language that stream incremental JSON events and reconstruct objects client-side
Compatibility layer that maps legacy streaming lines to new framed events
Unit tests showing structured-output validation and graceful deserialization errors
Documentation / short runbook for engineers integrating on Redwood Dedicated and Private
implementation_notes: Key design choices: 1) Use framed event envelope for all streaming responses: {event: 'delta'|'final'|'tool_call'|'tool_result'|'error', token: string?, payload: string (JSON-encoded)}. 2) For structured outputs, require optional JSON Schema reference (URI) on the request; SDKs provide small validator helpers that run during streaming and on final. 3) Tool registry is declarative: user provides a list of {name, argSchema, handlerSignature} at client init; runtime enforces type/shape before emitting tool_call events. 4) Compatibility: older clients that expect newline-delimited text will be supported by a compatibility mode that flattens framed events into text tokens with a small header prefix ("RW-LEGACY:TYPE:"). 5) Error handling: incremental validation failures emit a 'validation_warning' envelope and do not abort the stream by default.
python_interface_examples:
# Python example (simplified)
from typing import Callable, Dict
class ToolSpec:
    def __init__(self, name: str, arg_schema: str | None, handler: Callable):
        self.name = name
        self.arg_schema = arg_schema
        self.handler = handler
# streaming handler signature
def on_event(evt: Dict):
    if evt['event'] == 'delta':
        apply_delta(evt['payload'])
    elif evt['event'] == 'tool_call':
        args = json.loads(evt['payload'])
        result = tools[evt['payload_name']].handler(args)
        # SDK sends 'tool_result' back to runtime
# usage
client = RedwoodClient(tools=[ToolSpec('annotate', 'https://schemas.../annotate.json', annotate_handler)])
client.stream({'model': 'rw-3b', 'schema': 'https://schemas.../resp.json'}, on_event)
compatibility_notes: Migration guidance: - Legacy streaming clients that parse raw tokens can use the SDK compatibility flag to receive 'RW-LEGACY' prefixed lines. - Encourage migration to framed envelopes: this enables explicit tool_call/tool_result events and structured output validation. - For customers on Dedicated/Private, the edge router will support a toggle that rewrites outbound frames into legacy flattening at the tenant level to avoid client upgrades during rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests per language for: 1) event envelope parsing and reassembly of final JSON object; 2) schema validation injected mid-stream and on final; 3) tool registry enforcement (reject mismatched arg shape before tool_call); 4) compatibility flattening mode; Integration: small reference app that performs a multi-step chat where the model requests a 'db_query' tool, the SDK intercepts tool_call, runs handler, and returns tool_result events. Performance test to ensure validation overhead <5% p50 latency on streaming path.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge SDK API and examples into sdk repo behind feature flag. 2) Publish beta packages for TS/Py/Go and run internal dogfood apps for 2 weeks. 3) Flip default framing on hosted API with tenant-level opt-out for 30 days. 4) After monitoring and fixes, make framed events the default and deprecate RW-LEGACY flattening in 6 months.
qa_checks: Smoke test example apps on Hosted and Dedicated
Run compatibility mode against legacy tokenizers
Manual review of error/warning envelopes handling
Sign-off from SDK docs and DX leads
